title.narrative: Integrated Multi-Sector assistance to IDPs in Abiye-Adi town of Central Zone, Tigray Region.

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtThe project is focused on addressing the needs of individuals who have been displaced due to the conflict in the Tigray Region, specifically in the Abiye Adi town. The current displaced population includes individuals who have been forced to leave their homes from various areas within Tigray, as well as refugee returnees from Sudan. There are eight collective sites within the woreda where an estimated 48,526 individuals are currently residing, often in schools, rented accommodations, and other public areas. Unfortunately, these displaced individuals lack access to basic humanitarian services including shelter, medical and health services, WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene), and food. The limited presence of partners and humanitarian assistance has led to an increasingly challenging situation in the area.ltbrgtThe primary objective of the project is to provide dignified, rights-based integrated multi-sectoral humanitarian assistance to the displaced and conflict-affected populations to address their immediate life-saving needs. This includes providing safe and inclusive access to essential services and contributing to a well-coordinated response that ensures integration and mainstreaming of gender, protection, and accountability to affected people (AAP), and (PSEA) in the overall implementation of proposed sectors. The project will focus on providing humanitarian support in the areas of Shelter, WASH, and Multi-purpose cash assistance. It is expected that the most vulnerable beneficiaries will receive comprehensive support, including shelter options, with particular attention to addressing disability and potential protection risks.ltbrgtThe living conditions within the collective sites lead to various health issues, including crowded shelter environments, which are contributing to the spread of health problems within the population. The prevalence of scabies and malaria remains critical, and there are also protection concerns and gender-based violence (GBV) due to overcrowded shelter conditions.ltbrgtThe project aims to mitigate these risks and protection issues by providing alternative shelter solutions, conducting cash assistance for rent, and distributing bedding materials. The WASH component of the project aims to ensure equal and sustained access to reliable, safe water, appropriate sanitation, and hygiene services for the displaced populations.ltbrgtThe proposed activities of the project are aligned with sectoral objectives and have been developed based on the applicant's field presence and experience in the target locations. A community-based targeting criteria, informed by jointly agreed inclusion and exclusion criteria, and a community-led verification process overseen by NRC, will be implemented to ensure the inclusion of the most vulnerable displaced populations, promoting cohesion and peaceful co-existence between IDPS and host communities.
